methods.label: Count shaded-unshaded pairs
methods.explanation:
The diagram shows rows of \(1,3,5,7\) squares: each step down makes the row two squares longer. Because every row starts unshaded and alternates, it consists of one initial unshaded square followed by shaded-unshaded pairs.

Each step down adds one such pair. Row \(1\) has no pairs, so row \(n\), for a positive integer \(n\), has \(n-1\) pairs. Each pair contains exactly one shaded square, and every shaded square belongs to one pair. Therefore, row \(37\) contains
\[
37-1=36
\]
shaded squares, choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
